info.name: PodcastGenerator: OpenRouter speech
info.description:
Hand-run requests for OpenRouter's text-to-speech endpoint, `POST /api/v1/audio/speech`, with the model the app uses (`google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview`, voice `Umbriel`).

Set the collection variable `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to your own key (Postman: collection Variables tab, or better, an environment marked as a secret). Never commit a real key: this file holds only the variable name.

Sources: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/tts and https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation .

variable.description: Your OpenRouter API key. Leave empty in the file.

body.raw:
{
  "model": "{{model}}",
  "voice": "{{voice}}",
  "response_format": "pcm",
  "input": "# AUDIO PROFILE: The Host
## A late-night community radio presenter for a small, strange desert town.

## THE SCENE
A small, dim radio booth after dark. A single lamp, a microphone, a faint hum of equipment. The host reads the evening's
announcements to the town with total calm, as if this were the most ordinary broadcast in the world.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: Deadpan and warm. The host is completely at ease and treats strange, ominous or bureaucratic news as routine
civic business. No dramatic emphasis on frightening words, no spooky effects, no announcer bombast. Intimate, as if
speaking to a neighbor. Occasional quiet, more personal asides.
Pacing: Slow to moderate, steady and unhurried. A beat of silence after short declarative lines and before a change of
subject. Lists are read evenly.
Accent: Neutral, natural American English, no exaggerated regional features.

#### TRANSCRIPT
Good evening, listeners. The sky above our town is a particular shade of purple tonight. We will now continue with the news."
}

request.description: The app's prompt layout (audio profile, scene, director's notes, then the transcript; see docs/style-guide.md section 9.1), with a short transcript. Verified: the profile, scene and notes are used for direction and were not read aloud in this call. The response body is raw audio, not JSON: signed 16-bit little-endian PCM, one channel, 24000 Hz (the Content-Type header reads `audio/pcm; rate=24000; channels=1`). Use Send and Download, then open the file as raw audio. Each call costs real money (about $0.03 per minute of audio at $20 per million output tokens, 25 tokens per second of audio). This collection is for trying calls by hand. It is not part of `dotnet test` or CI, and the coding agents do not run it.
